Gear

Chokes

  1. What a choke is
    6 min★ Start hereSporting™Compak® SportingInterpreter

    A choke is a narrowing of the barrel at the muzzle that keeps the shot together. It decides how wide the pattern is at the target, and the rules of Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting say when you may change it.

  2. Fixed and interchangeable chokes
    5 minSporting™Compak® Sporting

    Chokes are either machined into the barrel for good or screw-in tubes you can change. Both options, and when the rules of Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting let you change them.

  3. Choke names, constrictions and markings
    6 minSporting™Compak® SportingInterpreter

    From cylinder to full: typical constrictions in millimetres and thou, the 1/4–1/2–3/4 fractions and the star marks used in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting. Values are approximate and differ between makers.

  4. Which choke for which distance
    5 minSporting™Compak® Sporting

    A rough guide to chokes for close, medium and far targets in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting, plus advice for beginners.

  5. Steel shot and chokes
    5 minSporting™Compak® Sporting

    Steel shot is hard and does not squeeze in the choke, so it patterns tighter. Which chokes suit it, how to read the proof marks, and what this means at Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting grounds that require steel.

  6. Pattern testing and choke care
    5 minSporting™Compak® Sporting

    How to check your pattern on a plate, how to clean and grease chokes, and why Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting shooters do not fire a multichoke gun without a choke.

    7 minSporting™Compak® Sporting

    5 minSporting™Compak® SportingFirst competition
